sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Dadhi Bal Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri D.B. Yadav, learned counsel for the applicants; Sri Padmakar Rai, learned A.G.A. for the State; and Sri Radha Krishna Yadav, learned counsel for opposite party No.2, who has filed vakalatnama today and the same is taken on record.

2. The instant application has been filed to quash quash the entire proceeding of case No. 5279 of 2022, case crime No. 440 of 2021, under Section 498A, 323, 506, IPC and 3/4 DP Act, P.S. Ghosi,
District Mau.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that dispute between the parties is matrimonial in nature and both the parties have settled their dispute amicably and entered into a written compromise.
It has been requested that the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
4. Though learned counsel for opposite party No.2 did not dispute the above fact, learned AGA states that the impugned proceeding cannot be quashed until the aforesaid compromise is verified.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the applicants are directed to file the original deed of compromise before the court below within a period of 15 days from today.

6. In case such a compromise is filed by the applicants, the court below will verify the said compromise after summoning the parties within a period of two months from the date of filing the compromise and after verification, the court below will dispose of the impugned proceeding in accordance with law.
7. For a period of two and a half months or till verification of compromise, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
8. However, the parties are at liberty to file a fresh application under Section 528 BNSS to quash the impugned proceeding on the basis of verified copy of compromise, if need arises.
9. With the aforesaid direction, the present application is disposed of.
